policy: An entry is permitted only for an intentionally defensive boundary where the exception is logged or the caller receives an explicit degraded/unknown result. Do not use this file to make a readiness gate green without owner review.

entries.reason: Rollback is best effort during a connection-loss poll. The caller records the original transient error, retries the probe, and the connection is discarded if it cannot roll back; no success is returned from this handler.

Custom-role validation degrades to built-in role names when the custom_roles table is absent (pre-migration deployments). The caller then rejects unknown role names with 422, so the degraded result is explicit rather than silent; no custom role is fabricated. (2026-10-16: location re-keyed after a line shift from the round-70 client-IP wiring import; the handler itself is unchanged.)

Role-name cleaning degrades to the built-in VALID_ROLES set when the custom_roles table cannot be read (pre-migration or schema drift). Assignment of an unresolvable name then falls back to the viewer default rather than storing an unvalidated role string; the API layer still 422s unknown names first.

Revision-walk probe: an unknown revision id (stamped or pruned history) stops the linear walk instead of raising. The caller then records the version move as a single linear_walk=false audit row rather than dropping it, so the degraded result is an explicit audit entry, never a silent success.

Pre-migration version probe: an unreadable/absent alembic_version state degrades to None so the post-migration audit hook records from_version=null honestly. The migration run itself is unaffected; no success is fabricated from the failed probe.

The Elasticsearch document-count probe inside _projection_lines: one unreachable projection store must not silence the rest of the /metrics surface. The failure is logged (projection_doc_count_unavailable) and the degraded result is explicit — the documents gauge is absent, never a fabricated count. (Line-keyed; re-key if the file shifts, the handler is the inner documents-count probe.)

The suspicious-access recorder runs inside the login-FAILURE path: a broken monitor must never block a refusal (that would turn a detector into a denial-of-service lever). The failure is logged (auth_monitor_record_failed) and the refusal proceeds regardless — the degraded result is an unrecorded observation, never a fabricated one.

The auth-monitor probe inside _auth_lines: the window is process state and must never take /metrics down with it. The failure is logged (auth_monitor_metrics_unavailable) and the degraded result is explicit — the gauges are absent, never zero-by-default. (Line-keyed; re-key if the file shifts.)
